A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DDOT study. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding methods, tables, algorithms, and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original DDOT experiments on One-Billion-Word, Yelp, and CodeParrot, including ablations, timing measurements, and appendix diversity results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and additionally displays no-OT inference trajectories in Figure 5.

M1.justification: The DDOT architecture and per-set OT mechanism remain. However, the reported position loss changes from Q_t-weighted MSE in v1 Equation 6 to unweighted MSE in v2 Equation 9. This is a limited objective revision; the PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both versions use FineWeb-Edu for initial fine-tuning and retain One-Billion-Word, Yelp, and Python CodeParrot evaluations with the same random/block infilling coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same methods: LC and PoP, the listed AR/NAR baselines in Table 3, and CBART in the appendix diversity comparison. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: v2 Algorithm 1 permits uniform terminal grids during training, whereas v1 Algorithm 1 specifies random sampling only. This revises the documented training procedure, although v2 Section 4.4 still specifies random sampling, leaving the option's experimental use unresolved. Other listed evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 5 adds scaled and unscaled inference trajectories without OT, supplementing the existing with-OT plots. v1 discussed these trajectories without displaying them. The numerical OT, model-size, loss-weight, and sampling-step analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The revision introduces no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 2–8 and existing plotted data retain their values; Figure 5 adds qualitative results. The appendix size-summary now says uniform initialization consistently outperforms random, although unchanged Table 6 contains reversals, including small-model One-Billion-Word BLEU-2 of 15.5 versus 15.7.

T1.justification: v2 repairs the absorbing-mask CTMC specification and adds explicit injective response-matching definitions and solver time/memory bounds in Sections 3–4. These refine the existing mathematical framework without introducing a new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central claims remain flexible-length infilling through joint token/position denoising, improved diffusion-baseline performance, and competitive NAR performance. Although the abstract drops 'first,' that novelty claim remains in the contributions and conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explicit argument that autoregressive whole-sequence regeneration wastes computation and explains OT efficiency through sorting and dynamic programming without dense cost matrices. The stated backbone-performance and KV-cache limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies the response-OT solver, prompt clamping, pad handling, and fuller training pseudocode, and adds a project-page link. These expand documentation rather than establish a replacement implementation. The code-release promise, hardware information, and numerical hyperparameter table remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds Needleman and Wunsch (1970), removes Cuturi (2013), Ho et al. (2020), Hoogeboom et al. (2021), and Karras et al. (2022), and sharpens the distinction between sample-level and minibatch OT. Most research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: The paper undergoes extensive language editing and substantial method-section restructuring into six subsections. The training algorithm moves from Appendix A.5 into the main text with expanded steps, while appendix results are regrouped and explanations extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 adds the two-panel Figure 5, relocates and reformats Algorithm 1, reflows appendix plots, and corrects trajectory captions from velocities to positions/training targets. Existing diagrams, result-table structures, and plotted data are largely retained.

improvement.justification: Clearer matching and pad-handling specifications, expanded pseudocode, and the missing no-OT visualization make v2 easier to understand and reproduce. These gains are limited by unresolved training-description inconsistencies, including conflicting learning-rate and loss-weight settings, and the overstated uniform-initialization summary accompanying Table 6.
